hints.title: Keep the whole real domain
hints.body: The implication must hold for every real x less than k, including very negative values. Such values may have large positive squares.
hints.recap: A universal condition cannot silently restrict x to positive inputs.
hints.pitfall: Testing only values near k overlooks most of the allowed half-line.
hints.pause: Try to make the premise true while making the square at least k.

recall.reminder: Search for a counterexample that satisfies the premise.

hints.title: Handle nonpositive parameters
hints.body: For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, compare the square of an allowed nonzero real input with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></math>. Choose the input so the strict premise also holds.
hints.recap: The input chosen to test a universal claim may depend on the fixed parameter.
hints.pitfall: Check the premise explicitly instead of using an arbitrary negative number.
hints.pause: Build a witness or proof settling all nonpositive parameter values.

recall.reminder: The input chosen to test a universal claim may depend on the fixed parameter.

hints.title: Handle positive parameters
hints.body: For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, construct a negative input whose magnitude is greater than both <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></math>. Write your choice in terms of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></math>, then test the premise and the strict conclusion separately.
hints.recap: You may choose the test input after the parameter has been fixed.
hints.pitfall: A negative input alone is not enough: verify the size of its square for the entire parameter case.
hints.pause: Specify your input, prove both comparisons for every positive parameter, and combine this with the nonpositive case.

recall.reminder: You may choose the test input after the parameter has been fixed.

solution:
If k≤0, x=k−1 satisfies x<k but x2>0≥k. If k>0, x=−k satisfies x<k but x2=k.

Every real k therefore has a counterexample to the proposed implication. No real values: answer A.
knowledgePattern: Universal implication defeated by sufficiently negative inputs
